editorial:
Retirement sounds great until you actually live it. That's the starting point for Ben Whittaker, a 70-year-old widower who feels lost without a daily purpose. When he lands a senior internship at a fast-growing online fashion company, he ends up working under Jules Ostin, the young founder who barely has time to breathe. The movie mixes workplace comedy with a sweet cross-generational friendship, and the warm tone makes it easy to settle into.

Robert De Niro brings charm and quiet humor to Ben, while Anne Hathaway makes Jules feel real and relatable. The pacing is gentle but never boring, and the humor comes from small moments rather than big gags. Some side plots feel a little thin, and the story wraps up a bit too neatly. Still, if you want a cozy, feel-good movie night, this one delivers. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Jules faces pressure to step down as CEO and let someone else run her company. Ben gently reminds her that she built something special and shouldn't give it up. She decides to stay in charge and keep growing the business. Ben remains her trusted intern and friend, and the movie closes on a warm, hopeful note about purpose at any age.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartwarming comedies and stories about unlikely friendships.
